'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|Crimea attacks]]
***[[Ukraine]]'s military says that its [[missile]] strikes near [[Yevpatoriya]] and [[Chornomorske]] in [[Russian occupation of Crimea|Russian-occupied]] [[Crimea]] damaged three [[Russia]]n [[Anti-aircraft warfare|air defense systems]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-says-it-hit-russian-air-defence-systems-occupied-crimea-2024-06-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defence Ministry]] says that [[Russian Armed Forces|its forces]] have recaptured the village of [[Staromaiorske]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://fakti.bg/en/world/887531-russia-has-announced-that-its-forces-have-taken-control-of-staromayorske-a-village-in-southeastern-ukraine (Fakti)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-takes-control-staromaiorske-eastern-ukraine-defence-ministry-says-2024-06-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***The [[United States]] lifts a ban on sending U.S. weaponry to Ukraine's [[Azov Brigade]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2024/06/10/azov-brigade-ukraine-us-weapons/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of El Fasher]]
***The last remaining operational hospital in [[Al-Fashir]], [[North Darfur]], closes down after being stormed and looted by the [[Rapid Support Forces]], according to [[Médecins Sans Frontières]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/10/last-hospital-in-north-darfur-capital-sudan-closes-after-paramilitary-attack (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 50 people are killed and an unknown number are kidnapped, including women and children, when gunmen attack the village of Yargoje in [[Katsina State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/06/10/nigeria-gunmen-kill-50-in-raid-on-northwest-village (Al Arabiya)]
*[[Somali civil war (2009–present)|Somali civil war]]
**At least 55 people are killed and 155 others are injured in fighting between the [[Dir (clan)|Dir]] and [[Marehan]] clans in central [[Somalia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/fighting-between-central-somalia-clans-kills-least-55-residents-say-2024-06-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Brazil wildfires]]
**It is reported that wildfires have burned around {{conv|32000|ha|acre}} of tropical wetland in [[Brazil]]'s [[Pantanal]] so far this year, a 935% increase in the number of fires that occurred in the same period last year. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crgg7rnlrylo (BBC News)]
*[[2024 Chikangawa Dornier 228 crash]]
**An aircraft carrying [[Malawi]]an [[Vice-President of Malawi|Vice-President]] [[Saulos Chilima]] and nine others is reported missing while flying from [[Lilongwe]] to [[Mzuzu]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4nn0zkq79ko (BBC News)]
*Forty-nine migrants, mostly from [[Ethiopia]] and [[Somalia]], are killed and 140 are missing after their boat capsizes off the coast of [[Yemen]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/11/dozens-dead-missing-in-migrant-boat-sin-king-off-yemen-un (Al Jazeera)]
*Three people are killed in floods and landslides in [[Hà Giang province]], [[Vietnam]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240610-flooding-and-landslides-kill-three-in-vietnam-s-north (France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**[[Poland]] announces a "no-go zone" in the [[Białowieża Forest]] in order to prevent migrants from crossing [[Belarus–Poland border|the border]] from [[Belarus]]. In response, concerns are raised about the potential impact on [[Tourism in Poland|tourism]] during the summer. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polish-border-no-go-zone-will-stop-tourists-well-migrants-locals-fear-2024-06-10/ (Reuters)]
*''[[Doe v. Chiquita Brands International]]'', [[Right-wing paramilitarism in Colombia]]
**After 17 years of litigation, [[Chiquita|Chiquita Brands International]] is found liable by a jury in [[Federal judiciary of the United States|United States Federal Court]] of financing the far-right paramilitary death squad [[United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia]] in the [[Antioquia Department|Antioquia]] and [[Magdalena Department]]s of [[Colombia]]. [https://earthrights.org/media_release/colombian-victims-win-historic-verdict-over-chiquita-jury-finds-banana-company-liable-for-financing-death-squads/ (EarthRights International)]
*Four American instructors from [[Cornell College]] in [[Iowa]], [[United States]], and one [[China|Chinese]] passerby are wounded in a stabbing attack at a park in [[Jilin City]], China. The perpetrator is arrested a day later. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/four-american-educators-stabbed-park-northeast-china-united-states-media-officials-beihua-university-jilin-4401156 (CNA)] [https://www.npr.org/2024/06/11/g-s1-3865/china-stabbing-us-iowa-college-instructors (NPR)]
*A [[Spain|Spanish]] court sentences three men to eight months in prison for [[Racism_in_Spain#Racism_in_football|racist chants]] directed towards [[Brazil]]ian football player [[Vinícius Júnior]]. [https://www.npr.org/2024/06/10/nx-s1-4998276/racist-chant-vinicius-spain-fans-punished (NPR)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
***The [[United States]] [[List of diplomatic missions of the United States|Consulate General]] in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]], is [[vandalism|vandalized]] by a pro-[[Palestinian]] activist. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/australia-pm-speaks-us-consulate-sydney-vandalized-gaza-war-rcna156277 (NBC News)]
**[[United Nations Security Council Resolution 2735]]
***The [[United Nations Security Council]] votes 14–0, with [[Russia]] abstaining, to back the ceasefire proposal outlined by [[US President]] [[Joe Biden]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/un-security-council-vote-plan-israel-hamas-ceasefire-2024-06-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Belgian federal election]]
**[[2024 Belgian government formation]]
***Following resignation of De Croo, government formation talks begin.[https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/10/belgium-seeks-new-government-after-pm-de-croo-resigns (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[New Flemish Alliance]] win the highest percent of votes in the federal election, followed by [[Vlaams Belang]] and the [[Reformist Movement]]. [https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/kies24/uitslagen/#kamer/het_rijk/belgie/ (VRT)]
**[[Belgian Prime Minister]] [[Alexander De Croo]] resigns after his party [[Open Flemish Liberals and Democrats]] loses to centre-right and conservative parties. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/10/belgium-seeks-new-government-after-pm-de-croo-resigns (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 Armenian protests]]
**Several large protests are held in [[Yerevan]], [[Armenia]], calling for [[Armenian Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] to resign due to Armenia ceding territory to [[Azerbaijan]] in the [[2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh|Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/10/armenian-protests-demand-pms-head-over-concessions-to-azerbaijan (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 Bulgarian parliamentary election]]
**No party attains a majority in the [[Bulgarian National Assembly]], with [[GERB]] attaining a plurality of seats. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2024/06/10/centre-right-bags-victory-in-bulgaria-national-and-eu-elections (Euronews)]
